A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GaGA and MG-Geo. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and included appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original geolocation evaluations, interaction experiments, training-stage ablations, human dialogue ratings, and qualitative results.

after.justification: V2 retains original geolocation, interaction, ablation, and human-rating results in its main text and appendix.

M1.justification: The architecture and projector-pretraining/QLoRA-finetuning procedure remain unchanged. V2 Section IV-C extends the described dialogue-generation pipeline with CoT Introspection: errors exceeding 25 km trigger ground-truth-guided revision of answers. V1's pipeline ended with prediction. CoT Deduction largely restates the existing self-questioning procedure.

E1.justification: V1 Table 9 evaluates both Im2GPS and Im2GPS3k; v2 Table VII retains only Im2GPS3k. The training sources, GWS15k, full OSV-5M test set, and 547-image interaction evaluation remain.

E2.justification: The Im2GPS3k comparison changes substantially: v1 Table 9 compares GaGA with PIGEON and GeoCLIP, whereas v2 Table VII retains PIGEON, removes GeoCLIP, and adds PlaNet, CPlaNet, ISNs, Translocator, and GeoDecoder. Other principal comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The retained experiments use the same benchmark sampling, hierarchical/direct evaluation procedures, distance thresholds, Geoscore, sample counts, and training hyperparameters. Added evaluation-mode labels and generation settings provide documentation; they do not establish changed experimental budgets or reruns.

E4.justification: V2 removes v1's detailed Clue-versus-Dialog diversity analysis and six additional qualitative cases in Figures 6–7, substantially reducing supplementary analysis. It adds a GWS15k distribution map. The training-stage ablation, full-test-set distribution check, interaction experiments, and human ratings are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Both versions report three experts assessing 50 dialogue samples, with identical Fleiss' Kappa values and rating counts. V2 explains and cites Kappa more fully but adds no uncertainty-estimation procedure, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Principal geolocation, interaction, ablation, and human-rating values remain unchanged; the full OSV-5M table only reduces numerical precision. Supplementary evidence changes substantially through added Im2GPS3k comparator results and removal of GeoCLIP, Im2GPS results, and qualitative outputs. Dataset statistics also change: v1 Figure 3(c) assigns 51k clues to Architecture, whereas v2 Figure 4(b) assigns approximately 51k to Road.

T1.justification: The visual projection and language-model equations are equivalent reformulations, and the Geoscore definition is unchanged. Neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs. The added correction procedure is methodological, not a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The GaGA and MG-Geo contributions and claimed country/city gains of 4.57 and 2.92 percentage points remain. V2's abstract and introduction additionally make explicit claims of real-time refinement through dynamic data integration, extending the practical scope of v1's dialogue-correction emphasis.

C2.justification: V2 extends the numerical-precision explanation to next-token training loss and explicitly discusses ineffective user guidance as a failure condition. It replaces the RAG-focused future discussion with temporal and sensor integration proposals. It also drops v1's explicit qualification about ranking methods across differing GWS15k reproductions, although reproduction markers remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds clue-prompt templates, metadata fields, manual-verification details, and GPT-4V decoding settings. Training hyperparameters remain identical. Conversely, it omits v1's exact ViT-L/14-336 and InternVL2-26B identifiers and hierarchical-evaluation pseudocode, despite retaining a pointer to that pseudocode.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning through text/social-network geolocation literature, a dedicated MLLM subsection covering specialized models such as LLaVA-Med and GeoChat, and new prompting, embodied-agent, and numerical-reasoning references. The existing visual-geolocation discussion largely remains.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, methodology, and dataset explanation; places the model before the dataset; and promotes several appendix evaluations into dedicated main-text subsections. It also changes LVLM terminology to MLLM, revises the author list, and adds biographies.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a journal layout, adds an architecture diagram, radar chart, distribution map, and boxed prompts, and redraws dataset charts. Tables are extensively restyled and relocated, with added evaluation-mode columns. Several appendix figures and the original dataset-example diagram disappear.

improvement.justification: V2 improves explanation of data construction and broadens research context, but removes Im2GPS evidence, the Im2GPS3k GeoCLIP comparison, detailed supplementary analyses, and reproducibility information. The principal results remain unchanged, and the added CoT Introspection procedure receives no separate evaluation. These substantive gains and losses leave the net effect on paper quality uncertain.
